title: Slow-roll trigger and SLO stress forecast
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational planner and KPI sheet for staged (slow) rollouts of product changes that could affect inference cost, latency, or quality. It combines: an explicit set of slow-roll triggers, forecasted SLO stress scenarios, monitoring signal thresholds, and a lightweight contingency playbook for the first 72 hours of a rollout.

TL;DR (one-line):
- Goal: Ship changes with predictable user-impact while keeping 99th-percentile latency increase < 25% and error-rate delta < 0.2pp during ramp.
- Primary trigger: sustained +15% token latency (p50->p99 tail shift) for 10m across >3 regions OR token compute cost increase >20% for 30m.

High-level rollout plan (slow-roll):
- Canary (0.5% of traffic, 30m) -> Stage A (2%, 2h) -> Stage B (10%, 6h) -> Stage C (33%, 12h) -> Full (100%).
- Pause/rollback gates at each stage if any trigger fires.

KPI table (tracked in charts / this sheet):
- Traffic percent (rollout stage): 0.5 / 2 / 10 / 33 / 100
- Request rate (RPS): baseline and observed (per-region)
- Token throughput (tokens/sec)
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms)
- 5xx rate (per 1k requests)
- Model-level decode cost ($/1000 tokens) and GPU utilization (%)
- Quality signals: hallucination rate sample (%), end-user rejection actions (/1000), automated rerank delta

Stress scenarios and forecast assumptions (quick summary):
- Scenario A (latency-sensitive): background latency increases with same QPS.
  - Assumptions: seq_len distribution unchanged; kernel warmup penalty +20% for first 100 requests per model shard.
  - Forecast: p99 up +18–30% for 30–60m depending on cache hit rate.
- Scenario B (cost impact): quantized model path increases single-token compute due to fallback to full-precision for rare ops.
  - Assumptions: 3% of op patterns trigger slow path leading to average cost +22%.
  - Forecast: per-token cost +18–25% leading to monthly cost delta estimate and breakeven for dedicated pool.
- Scenario C (quality regression): prompts with new input edgecases reduce top-1 accuracy leading to downstream rerates.
  - Assumptions: a 2–4pp increase in rerated outputs -> user-visible friction.

Primary slow-roll triggers (signal logic):
1) Latency tail trigger: p99 latency increase >= 15% vs baseline sustained for 10 minutes across >= 3 regions.
2) Error surge trigger: 5xx rate > baseline + 0.3 percentage points for 5 minutes.
3) Cost delta trigger: model decode cost per 1k tokens increases >= 20% for 30 minutes.
4) Quality sentinel: sampled hallucination rate increases >= 2pp on streaming QA prompts (sampled telemetry).
5) Manual safety open: any customer-reported P1 via CS or any legal/security hold.

Gate actions (when trigger fires at any stage):
- Immediate: pause rollout and notify on-call SRE and product ops (Slack channel #rollout-watch).
- 0–5m: capture slices (per-region p99/p95/p50, GPU util, cache hit, kernel-fallback counts, top error stacktrace).
- 5–15m: attempt benign mitigations (reduce batch size, pin previous model variant, scale up dedicated pool if allowed).
- 15–60m: if signals persist, perform automated rollback to previous model+config; open incident with severity based on user impact.

Owners & Contacts (quick roster):
- Product Ops owner: Maya Patel (owner of this doc)
- Rollout lead (executes ramp): Liam O'Connor
- SRE on-call (inference infra): Pager SRE rotation (see SRE schedule) -> primary: Priya Desai
- Model steward (quality): Noah Kim
- Customer escalation: Eva González (CS)

Monitoring dashboard names / slices to watch (exact Grafana panels):
- Inference/Latency/ByModel/p99: by region, by model shard
- Inference/Errors/5xx-rate: by route and customer tier
- Cost/Token/DecodePath: metric: tokens_decoded.billing_cost, tag: decode_path
- QA/Quality/Sampled-Hallucination: periodic sampler pipeline -> direct link in Confluence doc

Acceptance thresholds per-stage (quick matrix):
- Canary: No trigger allowed. Any trigger -> rollback.
- Stage A (2%): p99 <= baseline + 10% AND 5xx <= baseline + 0.15pp; if cost delta >20% we proceed only with finance approval.
- Stage B (10%): p99 <= baseline + 15% AND 5xx <= baseline + 0.2pp; quality sampler pass >= 98%.
- Stage C (33%): p99 <= baseline + 20% AND 5xx <= baseline + 0.25pp; quality sampler pass >= 99% (larger sample).

Runbook snippets (practical commands & quick checks):
- Collect traces: kubectl -n inference logs --selector=app=model-serving --since=15m --limit-bytes=1MB > traces-$(date +%s).log
- Cache diagnostics: curl http://cache-metrics.internal/kvcache?model=xxx | jq .hit_rate
- Pin variant: call rollout API: POST /api/rollouts/{id}/pin?variant=previous
- Emergency scale: terraform apply -var 'dedicated_pool_nodes=+4' (requires infra-ops approval)

Open questions / edge cases to resolve before full launch:
- Should cost delta trigger be measured per-customer as well as global? (pros: targeted rollbacks; cons: complexity in signal logic)
- What is the permitted finance approval window for temporary cost overrun during Stage A? Define limit and owner.
- Sampling strategy for quality signals: we need deterministic sampling keys for reproducible comparisons.

Post-roll analysis checklist (first 7 days):
- Day 0–1: capture baseline telemetry, annotate all trigger events and manual mitigations, initial incident writeup if any.
- Day 2–3: quality sampling deep-dive (1000+ prompts), human review of hallucination cases.
- Day 4–7: cost reconciliation vs forecast (delta broken down by decode path, token mix, and hardware utilization).
- Week 2: retro with cross-functional owners (product, SRE, infra, CS) and create follow-up tickets.

Quick appendices (links and artifacts):
- Smoke test checklist (link to runbook in Confluence)
- Sample Grafana panel JSON ids (copied into Confluence)
- Simulation notebook: GitHub link in linked_artifacts above

Notes to self / working items (TODOs):
- [ ] Add per-customer cost trigger logic (PRODOPS-1723)

- [ ] Bake deterministic sampling into telemetry pipeline (SRE-846)
- [ ] Schedule a 1-hour runbook rehearsal with SRE and model stewards before next rollout

Contextual references (quick):
- Background: recent rollout of vectorization-refactor raised p99 in a small set of shards; this doc consolidates learnings into a predictable slow-roll template.
- Non-exhaustive: this sheet is intentionally concise — full playbook and simulation notebooks live in linked_confluence and GitHub PR above.

If you're reviewing: please comment inline on acceptance thresholds and whether the finance gate should be automatic at Stage A.

-- Maya
